text: He was a raft-guard on the southern rivers before the council took him on to walk the council house's stilts by night.
He guards the streets by night in his turn with the city levy. He lodges with the boatwoman's household.
She is the mother of Poles-Upriver and knots fishing nets for the city's river fishers. She poled rafts herself until her grip failed.
She cleans, sorts and bundles the fellrunner feathers that the hunters of Murkwood bring to the household's stall.
She gathers lumberries in Last Seed and cooks for the pilgrims who lodge with her household.
She tends the eggs in the city's nest-pools and records every clutch with its parents and its hatch date.
She gathers herbs and roots in the swamp around the city for the household's stall.
She came to the wardens from the city levy and still drills with them on her days off.
He guards the streets by night for the levy and sleeps at its camp. He has no kin in the city.
The youngest warden, set to stand before the strongroom's iron door until dawn.
He keeps the gallery side of the house and sleeps through the day's noise of the hall below.
She lost nine teeth in a fight on the plank walks and has been called Nine-Teeth since. She guards the streets by night for the levy.
He walks the day watch of the city levy and lodges with the trader's household. He stops outsiders at the landing and does not explain why.
He nets trodh in the shallows of the river fork and sells them live at the market. Cooked trodh is poison, so his buyers eat them on the spot.
She grooms scales and polishes spines for customers who can pay. She works from a mat beside the market.
He tans hides at the smithy's rack and cuts leather straps for his partner's fittings.

She writes down every cargo landed at the river fork and who carried it, and keeps her tallies at the table of a quiet house by the city landing. Visitors come to her by word of mouth, and few in the city could say whose house it is.
She keeps a quiet room behind the market's stalls and lets it only to those who give the right word; two lanterns on her sill mean the room is free.
He builds the rafts for his partner's trade, lashing cane and sealing the joints with Hist-sap resin.
He is the oldest of the levy at the camp and leads the day watch. He settles quarrels among the guards before the naheesh hear of them.
He keeps the boatmen's lodge, where raft crews and the few outsiders eat and sleep. The crews named him for being the last awake in the lodge each night.
She gathers marsh-bird eggs in the forest around the city for the household's stall. She goes out at first light and is back before the market opens.
She hauls cargo from the rafts to the market stalls. In the pilgrim season she works from first light until after dark.
She is a naheesh and sits with the city's assembly of elders and tree-minders. She knows the sacred croaks of the Root Talk by heart.
She carves depth sticks and sells them to visitors who do not know the city's pools.
She mends the plank walks between the districts and replaces the boards that have rotted in the wet.
She unloads rafts at the landing and carries the goods to the households. The naheesh of the assembly set the share that each household receives.
He sells Hist-sap and swamp herbs from a stall with an alchemy bench and teaches the craft to apprentices who can pay. Sap is dear in Helstrom, because the tree-minders allow little to be taken.
He carves the grave-stakes that the city's grave-singers set over the dead.
He works the bellows and the grindstone at the smithy and is learning the forge from his father.
He keeps the root landing, where travellers climb down to board the rootworms. He knows each worm's temper and its route.
She is learning the tree-minder's work from her mother. She clears rot and creepers from the roots of the grove.
The council's head warden. He keeps the night's watch on the council house and the key to nothing but his own sword; the strongroom's key stays with the treasurer.
She is a grave-singer. She stakes the city's dead and sings the final song over them.
She buys from the raft crews and the rootworm riders and sells Murkwood feathers, sap, eggs and river fish from her market stall. Outsiders named her for the way in which she weighs their coin.
He fishes with his mother between his turns in the levy. He serves his next turn in Hist-Tsoko, when pilgrims crowd the city.
She pickles frog's eyes for the market. In Helstrom they are a delicacy and a cure for a sour stomach.
She serves the day watch of the levy and lodges with Kuxeesh's household. At the landing she searches every outsider's pack.
He builds the plank walks and stilt footings between the districts of the city. He also trains living wood into walkway posts, which takes years.
She collects the sap that the tree-minders release for sale and carries it home in sealed gourds.
She poled rafts on the Panther River for most of her life. Now she mends nets on the household's landing.
She meets the pilgrims who come for the Root Talk in Hist-Tsoko and finds them floor space in the city. Out of season she hires out as a river guide.

She served the Toh-Reel-Ka at Fort Chalkmoth for many years and is now the officer over Nesh-Deeka. She lodges in Nesh-Deeka's house and stands at the back of its room whenever the order has work there; in the city she passes for a raft-pilot from the northern rivers.
She traps fellrunners in Murkwood for their feathers and sells them to the stalls at the market.
He guards the streets by night for the city levy and lodges at the smith's house. The smith sharpens his blade for nothing.
He serves the day watch of the levy and lodges with the sap-seller. He was a raftsman before his tribe sent him to serve his turn.
She fishes the river fork from a one-person raft and sells her catch at the market.
He boils fleshfly emollient and scale balms for the stall. He sells most of them to raft crews before the flesh-fly season.
She digs black Heart-Mud from the pools between the roots and packs it into the walls of the city's houses.
She is a naheesh of the assembly and holds the naming secrets of the Chukka-Sei. She gives the city's young their names at their maturity trials.
She watches the back door to the river landing and counts the rafts that tie up below it after dark.
He seals roofs and raft seams with Hist-sap resin. He works in the dry spells and sits idle through the monsoon.
She owes a season of labour to a household that she wronged, by the ruling of the assembly's naheesh. She carries loads at the landing and keeps nothing of her pay until the season ends.
He works the forge at the market smithy with iron bought from the raft crews. The levy and the raft crews buy his blades and fittings and pay him well in goods.
She catches chirping frogs on the Panther River fork and sells them by their tone to the makers of frog pipes.
He rides the rootworms through the tunnels of the Hist roots to the villages of the basin. He brings back orders for the stall.
She is a tree-minder of the city grove and heals the sick at the tree-minders' hall. She sells tomes of Restoration and Alteration and teaches healing to those who ask.
Born in Pusbottom, she cooks for the council house and sleeps in a room of the council house. She owes a Lilmoth moneylender more than a cook can pay.
He takes in pilgrims for the Root Talk through the month of Hist-Tsoko. The rest of the year he fishes the river.
He cuts and shapes bark shingles for the city's roofs. He learned the trade on his father's crew.
She carries river water to the houses near the market in the weeks when the city spring is left untouched. She does not discuss the reason with outsiders.
She poles a cargo raft from Helstrom to the river villages of Truowa, Korydon, Marzai and Julo. Her passengers could not say her Jel name, so she answers to the name that they gave her.
He leads the town levy's day watch from the barracks and settles who walks which round. He stands at the landing end of the road, where Stormhold's buyers arrive.
She is the tree-minder of Jal-Veesa and calls the rootworm at the Hist pool for travellers bound for Helstrom. The tree's bark has dried and darkened this season.
He minds the fish weirs on the creeks and gathers the fee owed for each trap. From the weirs at night he sometimes sees lights among the ruins of Nenria, and he has told only Mizeera.
A ruin-warden of the Veesa-Teeleel, she teaches archery at the edge of the town between her turns at Gemin. She lives alone and stores her bowstrings in the rafters out of the damp.
She builds and caulks the reed boats that Sells-Dry-Fish sells at the jetty market. She learned the work from her mother and has taken no apprentice.
He carries rope and mats on his back along the road to Stormhold for buyers who will not come to the town on slack days. Taxhu-Neel says he walks that road more often than he poles the creek.
She is the root-herald of Jal-Veesa and speaks for the elders to Stormhold's buyers and the frontier screen. She hears all that is said in her house and repeats little of it.
He cuts sedge in the beds beyond the mud banks for the town's mats and boats. He poles out before dawn with his father's cutting knife.
She plaits mats from Kuxan-Deel's sedge and trades them to Sells-Dry-Fish at the jetty. She taught the knot she uses to several mat-makers in the town.
She dries and smokes fish at the racks on the road side. She says nothing of the lights Jeshun-Tal sees at Nenria, and she walks home by the ruin road.
She plaits the mats her mother sells at the jetty market and sets them out to dry on the racks by the creek. She can tell whose sedge a mat was cut from by the feel of it.
She takes her turns as a ruin-warden at Loriasel and comes home to the town between them. She was among those who took a looter with Ayleid goods, and she has not said what should be done with him.
She tends the elders' long house, sweeping its mats and laying out the guest mat for any traveller who asks for a bed. She and Vosh-Leera have eaten at one table for twenty years.
She walks the town by night for the levy and sleeps at the barracks by day. She walks the mud banks round the Hist pool, where the boat lanes are hardest to make out after dark.

She sells the town's reed boats, mats, rope and dried fish to Stormhold's buyers and runs the smoker's stall on the road side. She took her name from the buyers, and her birth name is not used in the town.
She twists sedge fibre into the rope for the boats Dazhul-Tei builds and sells what is left at the jetty. She hums while she works until anyone from Stormhold comes near.
He fishes eels and gar from the weir channels and brings them to the racks. He will not go near the channels where the crocodiles lie up after rain.
He hauls the day's catch from the weir traps to the fish racks and to his sister's stall. He has been bitten twice by gar and tells the story to any traveller who stops.
She lays the town's rope in long lanes of staked strands beside the creek, one order at a time. She sells it by the coil to Stormhold's buyers after slow bargaining.
He stands the night on the log walk and throws the offal in below the weir at dawn. He leaves the first fish of the dawn at the Hist-shoot post's landing and eats afterwards.
She reweaves the weir's fences after each flood and knows which stakes the crocodile has worked loose. She keeps the moss on the fences for the tree-minders and lets no one strip it.
He guts the eels and gar at the landing and throws the offal in below the weir, where the young crocodiles wait for it. He says the thief is a stranger from downstream.

She runs the eel and gar traps by day on her family's turn at the weir and carries the catch to Jal-Veesa's market. She has begun counting the traps each dusk, since they have been found empty at dawn.
He walks the slick log walk at dusk to count the traps with the day watch. He has fallen in twice this season and the others call him the eel.
He is serving his months of the Owing and cuts the long reed along the east bank. He and his brother Chee-jeem came on the same barge and have worked side by side since.
He binds the cut reed into bundles at the landing and counts the stack aloud as he ties each one. Ah-ja cuts what he binds.
He came in with the new gang and sleeps in the barge's hold with the others until the gang-master frees them each morning. He counts the months he still owes on his fingers.
He has worked more months than any other cutter at Ashgate, and newcomers ask him which bank to cut. He has been at Ashgate through two barges' coming and going.
He cuts the west reach where the mudcrabs come up the bank and carries a long pole to move them on. He talks to his tent-mates about the river and the mudcrabs.
He carries bundled reed from the landing stack down to the work barge and sleeps lightly, because the moored hull creaks at night. The barge leaves downriver full each month and comes back empty.
He gathers swamp fungus on the reed beds for the cook's pot and hones the cutters' knives on a flat stone at dusk. He pays for a place at the cook's fire with the fungus.
He leads his tent's cutting on the north reach and is first to point out the young crocodile lying in the reeds. He and his sister Chee-mar serve their months together.
She cuts beside Ra-tah and mends the tent's hides with sinew when the rain has loosened them. She leaves the first reed she cuts each month at the grave-stake by the gate.
He ties bundles at the landing across the stack from Chee-jeem and quarrels with him cheerfully about knots. He keeps the count of his days on a notched reed.
He is a Dunmer who cuts no reed and lives in the old post's stone hut with the strongbox key on his belt. He runs the gang's days and takes each new gang's names onto his roll.
She cooks for the reed gang and sells dried fish and lamp oil from her stall by the hut. Each new gang meets her first, at the spit pot in the barge's hold, before the gang-master takes their names.
He is the best hand with the cutting hook at Ashgate, and the others say the gang-master has never faulted his bundles. He tells visitors that the stone gate was once a road post's.
He keeps the cook's fire by the hut burning through the evening and carries lamp oil from Okeeh's stall to the tents. He sleeps through the barge's creak when his tent-mates do not.
He cuts the south reach, wading to the knee, and has learned where the mud is soft. He sings under his breath to keep the stroke.
He sets and lifts the eel traps along the weir, standing on the log boom with his feet wide. He learned the work from his father Hulzeeth and has yet to be bitten by a crocodile.
She cooks the day's eels and gar in the pot by the drying rack for everyone on the platform. She puts the heads aside for the young Hist's pool.
He watches the traps by night for the Sedge-Wardens of Jal-Veesa and counts every stranger who passes the reed hide to the west. His son Tsa-tah keeps the traps by day so that his father can sleep.
She works the eel traps by day and loads the catch for Urvyn Farm. She keeps the crocodiles off the log boom with a pole and a loud voice.

She has tended the weir's young Hist since it first broke from the roots of Jal-Veesa's tree, and she sells what it and the creek give. She speaks bluntly to strangers and has not slept well since its scar closed over the grey paste.
He poles a flat boat that takes the stacked jars to where the Unbound's crews collect them. He is paid by the trip and asks nothing of what the jars hold.
He carries the crews' jars in from the marsh to the longhouse wall. He is Hesseth's partner and the strongest back in the camp.
He is the hired Naga who stands at the fire by the longhouse and carries the key to the cage at the camp's edge. He took the Unbound's coin first and talked the others into it.
She counts the jars the crews bring and the coin the Unbound leave, and the others let her speak for the camp though no one leads it. She keeps the tally in knots on a cord.
He is the oldest of the camp and keeps the shrine of bones to Sithis. He says the jars bring nothing good and takes his share of the coin all the same.
He is the youngest of the band and fishes the creek below the camp. He joined for the coin and is quieter since the cage was filled.
She hunts the reeds round the camp for meat and hangs the best skulls on the trophy pole. She watches the cage more often than the guards do.
She guards the jars by day for the Unbound's coin. She once took tolls on the road from Stormhold to Helstrom and misses the travellers more than the coin.
